title: Rider Violet — detached composer shelf
question: This revision separates the prompt surface from a smaller tooling shelf and moves Git context into the conversation header. Review the suite, then choose a screen and note whether it is approved or needs adjustment.

options.label: Detached Command Shelf
options.lineage: Rider workbench + T3 work log + cw-code session context
options.thesis: The writing box now stands on its own; a shorter detached shelf below carries only prompt-scoped controls while Git moves into the session header.
options.viewport: A visible gap separates the full-width text box from the smaller left-aligned tool shelf; the send key balances it at far right.
options.risk: The narrower shelf must wrap or progressively collapse secondary controls at reduced center widths.

options.label: Settings Window
options.lineage: Rider settings clarity + focused overlay workflow
options.thesis: Configuration opens as a substantial focused window over an inert workbench, without making the project sidebar part of the settings layout.
options.viewport: The overlay contains only settings categories, provider roster, and provider detail. The workbench survives as subdued context around the edges.
options.risk: The large overlay must trap focus cleanly and keep background session activity visible but non-interactive.

options.label: Agents with Command Shelf
options.lineage: Rider workbench + full-width agent trace + detached prompt tooling
options.thesis: The Agents state inherits the smaller detached tool shelf and header Git context without disturbing its vertical roster and inspector.
options.viewport: The center composer and session header now match the primary state; the right pane remains optimized for agent supervision.
options.risk: The prompt shelf must retain enough contrast when the conversation canvas changes theme or brightness.
